# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1135

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃1135화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|흐릿한 달빛이 비쳐 오는 언덕 위, 홀연히 나타난 그의 모습은 실로 이질적이었다.
  6|
  7|비단 마삼보 뿐만이 아닌, 그들 모두에게.
  8|
  9|그리고 다음 순간, 창백한 입술 사이로 흘러나온 음성에는 앞서 그들이 느낀 이질감의 정체가 담겨 있었다.
 10|
 11|“그래, 역적질은 할 만하던가.”
 12|
 13|잔잔한 수면처럼 평온한 어조.
 14|
 15|하지만 그 안에 담긴, 군림하는 자만이 지닐 수 있는 위압감.
 16|
 17|그것은 품격(品格)이었다.
 18|
 19|어둠에 녹아든 새카만 장삼과 깊게 눌러쓴 죽립으로도 미처 가리지 못한.
 20|
 21|화려하기 그지없는 곤룡포(袞龍袍)나 면류관(冕旒冠) 없이도 자연스럽게 배어 나오는, 그야말로 타고난 품격.
 22|
 23|“오랜만이구나, 마 내관(內官).”
 24|
 25|까마득한 높이에서 굽어보는 듯한 하대.
 26|
 27|생각지도 못한 천자(天子)의 등장에, 내심 신음을 삼킨 마삼보가 가라앉은 음성으로 입을 열었다.
 28|
 29|“예까지 어인 일이시오, 황상(皇上).”
 30|
 31|천자가 담담하게 대꾸했다.
 32|
 33|“긴히 처리할 일이 있어 와 보았지.”
 34|
 35|“황도(皇都)를 비울 정도로 중요한 일이라 생각하시오?”
 36|
 37|“희한하군. 왜 짐이 황도를 비워도 될 만큼 철저히 준비해 두었다고는 생각하지 않느냐?”
 38|
 39|“……!”
 40|
 41|“한낱 역적 따위가 황도의 안위를 걱정할 필요는 없지. 적어도 황도십이궁(黃道十二宮)이 지키고 있는 한은.”
 42|
 43|침묵하는 마삼보를, 천자는 깊게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 응시했다.
 44|
 45|황도십이궁.
 46|
 47|황실을 수호하는 열두 명의 초절정 고수.
 48|
 49|비록 동천마군을 중심으로 벌어진 반역 이후로 그 숫자가 몇 남지 않았으나, 지금처럼 이동진의 위치만 알고 있다면 그들과 휘하 금위군만으로도 차고 넘치는 전력이었다.
 50|
 51|단, 어디까지나 적들이 황도를 친다는 가정하에서만.
 52|
 53|“허장성세(虛張聲勢)는 그만두어라. 애당초 황도를 노릴 계획이었다면, 네놈과 짐이 이리 마주할 일은 벌어지지 않았을 테니. 그렇지 않느냐?”
 54|
 55|정곡을 찌르는 한 마디에, 마삼보는 조용히 메마른 입술을 핥았다.
 56|
 57|천자의 말은 사실이었다.
 58|
 59|괴조(怪鳥)들로부터 정보를 입수한 그 순간, 마삼보는 황도라는 두 글자를 뇌리에서 깨끗이 지웠다.
 60|
 61|만약 황도를 함락시키고 천자를 손에 넣는다면 천하를 무릎 꿇릴 수 있겠지만, 그보다는 이미 크나큰 전력의 공백이 드러난 중원 무림이 훨씬 탐나는 먹잇감이었으니까.
 62|
 63|빠르고 편한 길을 놔두고 어려운 길을 택할 이유는 없었다.
 64|
 65|그리고, 이와 같은 마삼보의 착각이야말로 가장 커다란 패착(敗着)이었다.
 66|
 67|“……제법이구나, 주체(主體).”
 68|
 69|천자의 본명을 입에 담는 것은 그 자체로 대역죄.
 70|
 71|하지만 마삼보는 아랑곳하지 않고 말을 이었다.
 72|
 73|그는 지금껏 단 한 순간도 스스로를 천자의 신하라 생각하지 않았으니.
 74|
 75|다만 더는 물러설 길이 없는 이 상황 속에서, 아직 해결되지 않은 의문에 대한 답을 얻고자 할 따름이었다.
 76|
 77|“도대체 어찌 알았느냐. 이곳의 위치를.”
 78|
 79|그리고 그 물음에 답한 것은, 천자가 아닌 제갈풍이었다.
 80|
 81|“이 년.”
 82|
 83|“뭐?”
 84|
 85|“아, 욕한 것이 아니니 오해는 말게. 뭐 자네가 고자라는 사실은 알고 있지만, 그래도 겉보기에는 확실히 년이 아니라 놈이니까.”
 86|
 87|얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳은 마삼보를 향해 빙긋 웃은 제갈풍이 재차 입을 열었다.
 88|
 89|“이동진의 존재를 알아차린 후부터 온 천하를 이 잡듯이 뒤졌지. 정확히는 이 년이 아니라 일 년 반 정도겠군.”
 90|
 91|“……!”
 92|
 93|“오, 그래. 나도 처음 이 미친 짓거리를 시작할 때는 딱 지금 자네와 같은 표정이었지. 가솔들의 경우에는 더 안 좋았고, 검왕(劍王)과 권왕(拳王) 선배는 내 목을 조르려고 들더군. 지금은 돌아가시고 없는 도왕(刀王)께서는 그보다도 심했어.”
 94|
 95|안 좋은 기억을 떠올리며 목덜미를 쓰다듬는 제갈풍의 모습을, 마삼보는 믿을 수 없다는 듯이 바라보았다.
 96|
 97|“뒤졌다고? 그것도 십왕(十王)들까지 동원해서?”
 98|
 99|“어떤 심정인지 충분히 이해하네. 하지만 뭐, 우리가 그것 말고 달리 뭘 할 수 있었겠나?”
100|
101|제갈풍은 한숨과 함께 손에 쥔 학우선을 살랑살랑 흔들었다.
102|
103|사실 처음 한두 달은 지옥이나 다름없었다.
104|
105|아니, 그보다 더했다.
106|
107|차라리 지옥에는 군데군데 유황불이라도 피어오르지, 그들은 끝없는 망망대해(茫茫大海) 한복판에 표류당한 기분이었으니까.
108|
109|그러나 첫 결실을 보기까지는 그리 오래 걸리지 않았다.
110|
111|“석 달 만에 한 곳을 발견했지. 안휘성의 황산(黃山) 깊숙이 숨겨져 있더군. 다행히 그다음부터는 찾는 속도가 훨씬 빨라졌어.”
112|
113|그 모든 것은 매우 극비리에, 그것도 은영각(隱影閣)의 선별 과정을 통해 확실히 검증받은 이들만을 통해 진행되었다.
114|
115|구파일방과 오대세가의 일원이라 할지라도 예외는 없었다.
116|
117|아니, 설령 장문인이라 해도 다르지 않았다.
118|
119|그들은 오직 한 사람, 무림맹주의 명령을 따랐고 각자에게 주어진 임무를 충실히 수행했다.
120|
121|궁기방의 스승이자 개방의 방주인 만리추행(萬里追行)은 하오문과 함께 믿을 만한 수하들을 총동원하여 이동진이 존재할 만한 위치를 찾았고, 제갈세가와 은영각의 지자(智者)들은 그들이 가져온 정보를 바탕으로 더욱 구체적인 장소를 유추해 냈다.
122|
123|“아무리 어려운 문제라도 풀이 방법을 안다면 능히 답을 얻어낼 수 있지. 다행히 이동진의 위치를 찾는 과정 역시도 이와 같더군.”
124|
125|그것은 어릴 적부터 신동으로 이름 높았던 제갈풍에게도 매우 어려운 문제였지만, 그는 머지않아 풀이 방법을 알아냈다.
126|
127|인적이 드물고 유독 기의 흐름이 강하며, 최소 수백의 인원을 수용할 수 있는 면적에 풀숲이 형성되지 않는 곳.
128|
129|제갈풍은 이처럼 특정 조건을 갖춘 장소만을 선별했고, 그의 결정이 내려지면 제갈세가의 이름난 진법가들과 기감에 뛰어난 고수들이 직접 현장을 찾아 검증했다.
130|
131|이를테면, 남궁세가의 태상가주인 창천검왕이나 권왕과 같은 초절정 고수들이.
132|
133|“허나 아무리 애써도 부족함이 있더군. 나름대로 적지 않는 수였지만, 우리만으로 기밀을 철저히 유지하면서 이 드넓은 구주(九州)를 완벽하게 뒤지기에는 무리였거든.”
134|
135|한 치의 실수도 용납되어서는 안 되는 일이었다.
136|
137|아무리 단단한 성벽이라 해도, 붕괴는 아주 작은 하나의 균열에서 시작되는 법이니까.
138|
139|그런 의미에서 이동진은 그 자체로 거대한 화약고(火藥庫)나 다름없었다.
140|
141|단 하나만 터져도 천하를 불길에 휩싸이게 만들 수 있는.
142|
143|그러나 불과 몇 달 전 찾아온, 생각지도 못했던 도움의 손길에 제갈풍은 마음 한구석에 남아 있던 마지막 불안감마저 떨쳐낼 수 있었다.
144|
145|“어느 높으신 분이 맹주께 그러셨다는군. 도울 수 있는 일이 있다면 무엇이든 하시겠노라고. 덕분에 아주 큰 도움이 됐지.”
146|
147|제갈풍의 말에, ‘어느 높으신 분’이 입을 열었다.
148|
149|“제일 높으신 분, 이 맞지 않겠나?”
150|
151|“아, 결례를 용서하십시오. 폐하.”
152|
153|“물론 용서할걸세. 대역죄만 아니라면 무엇이든.”
154|
155|멍하니 제갈풍과 천자가 주고받는 대화를 듣고 있던 마삼보는 이를 악물었다.
156|
157|‘당했다, 그것도 완벽하게.’
158|
159|중원의 적들은 바로 이 순간만을 위해 인내해 왔던 것이 분명했다.
160|
161|찾아낸 이동진을 폐쇄할 능력이 있음에도 방치했고, 그 대신 완벽한 덫을 깔았다.
162|
163|사냥감이 군침을 흘리며 달려들 수 있도록.
164|
165|그리하여 마지막 근심마저 완전히 뿌리 뽑을 수 있도록.
166|
167|“앞서 보낸 선발대도 이런 방식으로 처리한 거였나?”
168|
169|마삼보의 물음에 제갈풍은 부드럽게 학우선을 흔들었다.
170|
171|“도착과 동시에 화산파(華山波)에 의해 전멸당했지. 그 빈자리는 맹주께서 이끄시는 무림맹의 정예가 채웠고.”
172|
173|“우리가 입수한 정보에는 분명 두 도적 놈들과 합류했다는 것이었는데.”
174|
175|“뭐 그리 어렵겠나. 비슷한 머릿수에 흑의(黑衣)만 걸치면 되는 일인데. 그에 대한 소문은 알아서 퍼져 나가기 마련이지. 실제로도 그랬고.”
176|
177|녹림맹과 장강수로맹에 합류했어야 할 일만의 광신도들은 그렇게 죽었다.
178|
179|장강수로맹의 선박에 몸을 싣기도 전에.
180|
181|그리고 해상왕 파륜은 그 사실을 철저히 숨겼다.
182|
183|그가 자신의 제자인 선화아(船火兒) 무송을 제압한 것 또한, 어디까지나 기밀을 지키려는 방편이었을 뿐이었다.
184|
185|사전에 계획을 듣지 못한 제자가 정의감에 불타 제멋대로 움직인다면, 애써 분리까지 해 둔 후미의 선박에 타고 있는 자들이 무림맹 소속이라는 사실이 알려질 위험이 있었으니까.
186|
187|“하지만 그전에 수적 놈들이 격파한 수백 척의 함대는 도대체…….”
188|
189|일순간, 마삼보는 문득 말꼬리를 흐렸다.
190|
191|서늘한 미소를 머금고 있는 천자의 모습이, 마지막 남은 의문에 대한 답을 알려 주었기 때문이었다.
192|
193|“과연, 그렇게 된 거였나.”
194|
195|마침내 모든 것을 깨달은 마삼보는 자신도 모르게 헛웃음을 터트렸다.
196|
197|잠시 잊었다.
198|
199|천자의 저 창백한 피부 속에는, 뜨겁고 붉은 피 대신 차가운 철혈(鐵血)이 흐른다는 사실을.
200|
201|“지금쯤 황궁의 뇌옥이 텅 비었겠군. 주체, 네놈의 농간이었느냐?”
202|
203|천자가 담담하게 대꾸했다.
204|
205|“그간 나라를 좀먹던 역적들이 워낙 많다 보니, 일일이 죽이는 것도 일이더군. 나름대로의 값을 치렀으니 그자들에게도 썩 나쁜 최후는 아니었을 것이다.”
206|
207|동천마군의 반란 직후 벌어진, 대국 역사상 두 번 다시 없을 대숙청(大肅淸).
208|
209|그중 아직까지 살아남아 처분을 기다리고 있던 수많은 죄인들에게 천자는 제안했다.
210|
211|법에 따라 일족과 함께 죽음을 맞거나 평생 노비로 살아갈 것인지. 혹은 가문이 진 오명을 조금이라도 벗겨 낼 것인지.
212|
213|당연하게도 대부분의 죄인들은 후자를 택했다.
214|
215|그들은 전신을 속박하던 사슬과 칼을 벗고, 떨리는 손으로 창칼을 받아 대국의 선박에 올랐다.
216|
217|자신들의 이 선택으로 피붙이 중 누군가는 살아남아 가문을 이으리라는, 천자의 약속을 끊임없이 마음속으로 되새기며.
218|
219|“그래, 어쩐지 예상했던 것보다도 쉽게 풀린다 했었지. 제아무리 썩어 빠졌어도 그 정도의 대패(大敗)를 겪는 건 확실히 이상한 일이었으니.”
220|
221|애당초 훈련받은 군인이 아니었으니, 수백의 함대와 화포가 있다 해도 전멸은 당연지사.
222|
223|그 수많은 죄인들을 먹잇감으로 던져 준, 오직 천자만이 벌일 수 있는 이 대담한 계획의 전말을 알게 된 마삼보는 실소할 수밖에 없었다.
224|
225|아니, 그래야만 했다.
226|
227|이미 모든 것을 포기한 듯한 실없는 웃음이 있어야, 자신에게 남은 마지막 기회를 감출 수 있었으니까.

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P92]
“There were so many traitors eating away at the nation that killing them one by one became a chore. They paid a price of their own, so it wasn’t such a bad end for them.”

[P93]
After the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s rebellion came a purge without precedent in the Great Nation’s history.

[P94]
The Son of Heaven had made an offer to the many prisoners who survived it and still awaited punishment.

[P95]
They could die with their families, as the law required, or spend the rest of their lives as slaves. Or they could lift even a little of the stain from their family names.

[P96]
Naturally, most chose the last option.

[P97]
Freed from the chains and restraints that bound them, they accepted spears and blades with trembling hands and boarded the Great Nation’s ships.

[P98]
All the while, they repeated the Son of Heaven’s promise to themselves: because of their choice, someone of their blood would survive to carry on the family name.

[P99]
“Right. No wonder it went more smoothly than I expected. Rotten as their forces were, it was strange for them to suffer a defeat that crushing.”

[P100]
They hadn’t been trained soldiers. Even with hundreds of ships and cannons, their annihilation had been inevitable.

[P101]
Now that he knew the full extent of the audacious plan—one only the Son of Heaven could have carried out, throwing all those prisoners to the enemy as bait—Ma Sanbao could only laugh.

[P102]
No. He had to laugh.

[P103]
A hollow laugh, as though he had given up, was the only way to conceal his last chance.

[P104]
*Not yet. It’s not over yet.*

[P105]
His mouth smiled. His eyes did not.

[P106]
Ma Sanbao swept his gaze around.

[P107]
On the hills encircling them, countless arrowheads poked quietly through the thick grass. He sensed his subordinates holding their breath, waiting for his command.

[P108]
*They outnumber us at least five to one. Maybe more.*

[P109]
It didn’t matter.

[P110]
If he could capture just one of the enemies who had prepared so thoroughly, he could turn this desperate situation around.

[P111]
No—he might do more than that. He might seize everything.

[P112]
That was what the Son of Heaven was worth.

[P113]
Besides, Ma Sanbao and his men had no other choice.

[P114]
“Now—!”

[P115]
It all happened in an instant.

[P116]
Ma Sanbao shouted and sprang from the ground.

[P117]
The taut bowstrings released their arrows all at once.

[P118]
And—

[P119]
*Whoosh!*

[P120]
Before the countless arrows, unable to match his speed, had even covered the ground behind him, a low whistle sounded above Ma Sanbao’s head.

[P121]
*No Shadow…!*

[P122]
Ma Sanbao clenched his teeth at the masked figure who had appeared in his path.

[P123]
It was him.

[P124]
Ma Sanbao had never seen his face clearly, but he knew of the Son of Heaven’s hidden bodyguard.

[P125]
The imperial household’s greatest assassin, who never even revealed his shadow, was bringing down a dagger wrapped in Force beneath the faint moonlight.

[P126]
Just as Ma Sanbao had expected.

[P127]
*Shhk!*

[P128]
With a gruesome sound of torn flesh, the blade sank into his forearm.

[P129]
Ma Sanbao paid it no mind. He thrust out his half-severed left hand and struck No Shadow.

[P130]
*Crack!*

[P131]
No Shadow went flying from the force of the blow. Ma Sanbao drove internal energy into the tips of his feet and released it.

[P132]
*Boom!*

[P133]
He shot down toward the hill like a falling star.

[P134]
The White Illusion Jiangshi Art, grown stronger still since the bloody battle at the imperial palace, let him forget pain and fear.

[P135]
“Zhu Di!”

[P136]
Ma Sanbao roared.

[P137]
A dozen or so arrows shot from his blind spots and buried themselves across his body. Zhuge Feng and Baek Yeon blocked his path. But his corpse-gray eyes remained fixed on one person alone.

[P138]
The Son of Heaven, his pale face still bearing the unmistakable signs of illness, just as it had the last time Ma Sanbao saw him.

[P139]
*Shhk! Thud!*

[P140]
*Crack!*

[P141]

[P142]

[P143]
*Slash!*

[P144]

[P145]
*Crack!*

[P146]
Ma Sanbao’s one remaining hand finally closed around what he wanted.

[P147]
The Son of Heaven’s throat.

[P148]
“Everyone, stop.”

[P149]
Silence fell.

[P150]

[P151]

[P152]
“Thank you. You came all the way here yourself, so—”

[P153]
*Thud.*

[P154]
Ma Sanbao blinked.

[P155]
Why?

[P156]

[P157]

[P158]

[P159]
*Crack.*

[P160]
The Son of Heaven slowly twisted the hand he had driven through the center of Ma Sanbao’s chest.

[P161]

[P162]
“…!”

[P163]

[P164]

[P165]

[P166]

[P167]
Even if it meant breaking a taboo, even if he might regret it one day, he would stay with his younger brother for as long as he could.

[P168]
And that choice had brought them to this moment.

[P169]
“Now I understand why Jin Taekyung gave me the White Illusion Jiangshi Art. It wasn’t just for me… It was for my brother, who would otherwise be left alone again.”

[P171]

*Crack!*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

Myriad-Mile Pursuit, Gung Gibang’s master and the Beggars’ Sect Leader, mobilized every trusted subordinate he could alongside the Lower District Sect to look for places where a Moving Formation might be hidden. The Zhuge Clan’s and Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s strategists used what they brought back to narrow down the locations.

[P55]
“No matter how difficult a problem is, you can find the answer once you know how to solve it. Fortunately, finding the Moving Formations worked the same way.”

[P56]
Even for Zhuge Feng, renowned as a prodigy since childhood, it had been an extraordinarily difficult problem. But before long, he worked out the method.

[P57]
He looked for places few people visited, where qi flowed with unusual strength, where there was room for at least several hundred people, and where no grass grew.

[P58]
Zhuge Feng selected sites that met those conditions. Once he made his choice, renowned formation masters from the Zhuge Clan and masters with exceptional Qi Sense went to verify them in person.

[P59]
Supreme Peak masters such as the Azure Sky Sword King, Grand Family Head of the Nangong Family, and the Fist King were among them.

[P60]
“But no matter how hard we tried, we didn’t have enough people. We had a fair number, but searching all nine provinces thoroughly while keeping the secret was beyond us.”

[P61]
Not a single mistake could be allowed.

[P62]
Even the sturdiest wall could begin to collapse with one tiny crack.

[P63]
In that sense, each Moving Formation was a vast powder keg. A single one going off could set the whole world ablaze.

[P64]
Then, a few months ago, help came from an unexpected source. Zhuge Feng could finally put the last of his worries to rest.

[P65]
“I heard a certain person of high standing told the Alliance Leader he’d do anything he could to help. And he was a tremendous help.”

[P66]
At Zhuge Feng’s words, the “person of high standing” spoke up.

[P67]
“Surely you mean the person of *highest* standing?”

[P68]
“Ah, forgive my discourtesy, Your Majesty.”

[P69]
“Of course. I’ll forgive anything short of high treason.”

[P70]
Ma Sanbao had listened blankly to their exchange. Now he clenched his teeth.

[P71]
*They got me. Completely.*

[P72]
The enemies in the Central Plains must have waited for this very moment.

[P73]
Though they could have shut down the Moving Formations they found, they had left them alone and laid a perfect trap instead.

[P74]
They had let their prey come running, mouths watering, so they could root out their last remaining concern.

[P75]
“Is that how you dealt with the advance party, too?”

[P76]
Zhuge Feng gently waved his feather fan.

[P77]
“Huashan wiped them out as soon as they arrived. The Murim Alliance’s elite, led by the Alliance Leader, took their place.”

[P78]
“Our information clearly said they’d joined those two bandit bastards.”

[P79]
“What’s so hard about that? We only needed a similar number of people dressed in black. Word was bound to spread on its own. And it did.”

[P80]
The ten thousand fanatics who were supposed to join the Green Forest Alliance and the Yangtze River Channel League had died before they ever boarded the league’s ships.

[P81]
And the Seafaring King, Pa Ryun, had kept the truth thoroughly concealed.

[P82]
Even subduing his disciple, Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song, had been a way to protect the secret. If Mu Song, who hadn’t been told the plan, acted on his sense of justice, he might expose the fact that the people aboard the rear ships—deliberately kept separate—belonged to the Murim Alliance.

[P83]
“But then what about the fleet of hundreds of ships the river bandits destroyed…?”

[P84]
Ma Sanbao trailed off.

[P85]
The Son of Heaven’s cold smile had given him the answer to his last question.

[P86]
“I see. So that’s what happened.”

[P87]
At last, Ma Sanbao understood everything. A hollow laugh escaped him.

[P88]
He had forgotten for a moment.

[P89]
Beneath the Son of Heaven’s pale skin ran cold iron blood, not hot red blood.

[P90]
“The palace’s underground prison must be empty by now. Zhu Di, was this your doing?”

[P91]
The Son of Heaven answered evenly.

[P92]
“There were so many traitors eating away at the nation that killing them one by one became a chore. They paid a price of their own, so it wasn’t such a bad end for them.”

[P93]
After the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s rebellion came a purge without precedent in the Great Nation’s history.

[P94]
The Son of Heaven had made an offer to the many prisoners who survived it and still awaited punishment.

[P95]
They could die with their families, as the law required, or spend the rest of their lives as slaves. Or they could lift even a little of the stain from their family names.

[P96]
Naturally, most chose the last option.

[P97]
Freed from the chains and restraints that bound them, they accepted spears and blades with trembling hands and boarded the Great Nation’s ships.

[P98]
All the while, they repeated the Son of Heaven’s promise to themselves: because of their choice, someone of their blood would survive to carry on the family name.

[P99]
“Right. No wonder it went more smoothly than I expected. Rotten as their forces were, it was strange for them to suffer a defeat that crushing.”

[P100]
They hadn’t been trained soldiers. Even with hundreds of ships and cannons, their annihilation had been inevitable.

[P101]
Now that he knew the full extent of the audacious plan—one only the Son of Heaven could have carried out, throwing all those prisoners to the enemy as bait—Ma Sanbao could only laugh.

[P102]
No. He had to laugh.

[P103]
A hollow laugh, as though he had given up, was the only way to conceal his last chance.

[P104]
*Not yet. It’s not over yet.*

[P105]
His mouth smiled. His eyes did not.

[P106]
Ma Sanbao swept his gaze around.

[P107]
On the hills encircling them, countless arrowheads poked quietly through the thick grass. He sensed his subordinates holding their breath, waiting for his command.

[P108]
*They outnumber us at least five to one. Maybe more.*

[P109]
It didn’t matter.

[P110]
If he could capture just one of the enemies who had prepared so thoroughly, he could turn this desperate situation around.

[P111]
No—he might do more than that. He might seize everything.

[P112]
That was what the Son of Heaven was worth.

[P113]
Besides, Ma Sanbao and his men had no other choice.

[P114]
“Now—!”

[P115]
It all happened in an instant.

[P116]
Ma Sanbao shouted and sprang from the ground.

[P117]
The taut bowstrings released their arrows all at once.

[P118]
And—

[P119]
*Whoosh!*

[P120]
Before the countless arrows, unable to match his speed, had even covered the ground behind him, a low whistle sounded above Ma Sanbao’s head.

[P121]
*No Shadow…!*

[P122]
Ma Sanbao clenched his teeth at the masked figure who had appeared in his path.

[P123]
It was him.

[P124]
Ma Sanbao had never seen his face clearly, but he knew of the Son of Heaven’s hidden bodyguard.

[P125]
The imperial household’s greatest assassin, who never even revealed his shadow, was bringing down a dagger wrapped in Force beneath the faint moonlight.

[P126]
Just as Ma Sanbao had expected.

[P127]
*Shhk!*

[P128]
With a gruesome sound of torn flesh, the blade sank into his forearm.

[P129]
Ma Sanbao paid it no mind. He thrust out his half-severed left hand and struck No Shadow.

[P130]
*Crack!*

[P131]
No Shadow went flying from the force of the blow. Ma Sanbao drove internal energy into the tips of his feet and released it.

[P132]
*Boom!*

[P133]
He shot down toward the hill like a falling star.

[P134]
The White Illusion Jiangshi Art, grown stronger still since the bloody battle at the imperial palace, let him forget pain and fear.

[P135]
“Zhu Di!”

[P136]
Ma Sanbao roared.

[P137]
A dozen or so arrows shot from his blind spots and buried themselves across his body. Zhuge Feng and Baek Yeon blocked his path. But his corpse-gray eyes remained fixed on one person alone.

[P138]
The Son of Heaven, his pale face still bearing the unmistakable signs of illness, just as it had the last time Ma Sanbao saw him.

[P139]
*Shhk! Thud!*

[P140]
*Crack!*

[P141]
There was no blood left to spill from a body already little different from a jiangshi. Only chunks of flesh and pieces of bone flew through the air.

[P142]
But his desperate will remained.

[P143]
*Slash!*

[P144]
Baek Yeon’s crescent-bladed polearm bit into Ma Sanbao’s left shoulder and sliced diagonally through his upper body.

[P145]
*Crack!*

[P146]
Ma Sanbao’s one remaining hand finally closed around what he wanted.

[P147]
The Son of Heaven’s throat.

[P148]
“Everyone, stop.”

[P149]
Silence fell.

[P150]
Before the Son of Heaven could draw the sword at his waist, Ma Sanbao had seized and immobilized him with lightning speed. He smiled faintly.

[P151]
Then he whispered into the ear of the Son of Heaven, whose pressure points he had struck.

[P152]
“Thank you. You came all the way here yourself, so—”

[P153]
*Thud.*

[P154]
Ma Sanbao blinked.

[P155]
Why?

[P156]
How could the Son of Heaven move after his pressure points had been struck?

[P157]
And why, now that they were face-to-face, was the Son of Heaven’s skin so much like his own?

[P158]
“…You. Don’t tell me—”

[P159]
*Crack.*

[P160]
The Son of Heaven slowly twisted the hand he had driven through the center of Ma Sanbao’s chest.

[P161]
“A few months ago, someone gave me a great gift. Something you know well.”

[P162]
“…!”

[P163]
“I thought long and hard about it. It was a blessing, but every bit as much a curse.”

[P164]
The Son of Heaven’s deliberation had not lasted long, though. His only remaining blood relative, the sole heir who would inherit the realm, had made him a request.

[P165]
“He told me to live a thousand years. He wanted us to stay together for a long time—not as Son of Heaven and heir, but as family.”

[P166]
For the sake of Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao—no, Imperial Younger Brother Zhu Bao—and his heartfelt wish, the Son of Heaven made his choice.

[P167]
Even if it meant breaking a taboo, even if he might regret it one day, he would stay with his younger brother for as long as he could.

[P168]
And that choice had brought them to this moment.

[P169]
“Now I understand why Jin Taekyung gave me the White Illusion Jiangshi Art. It wasn’t just for me… It was for my brother, who would otherwise be left alone again.”

[P170]
Then—

[P171]
“By the law of the Great Nation, I punish this traitor.”

[P172]
*Crack!*

[P173]
The Son of Heaven’s voice was the last Ma Sanbao would ever hear. The world before his eyes went black.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes
